checks.context: Without at-rest encryption, cache data (which often includes session tokens, user data, or query results) is stored in plaintext. Encryption must be enabled at creation time and cannot be added later.
Without TLS, all data between your application and the cache is transmitted in plaintext. This exposes session data, cached credentials, and application data to network interception.

checks.message: No access control configured for Redis/Valkey cluster
checks.context: Without access control, any client that can reach the endpoint can read and write all cached data. Use --user-group-ids (RBAC) to assign a user group with fine-grained permissions - this is the recommended approach for Redis 6+ and Valkey. RBAC supersedes the older --auth-token (AUTH) method and is flagged by AWS Config (elasticache-rbac-auth-enabled). AUTH is still supported but RBAC provides per-user command and key permissions.

checks.message: Prefer replication groups over standalone clusters for production
checks.context: Standalone cache clusters have no failover capability. A single node failure causes complete cache loss. Use replication groups with Multi-AZ for production workloads.

checks.message: In-transit encryption not enabled on cache cluster
checks.context: Without TLS, all data between your application and the cache is transmitted in plaintext, exposing session data and cached credentials to network interception. Supported for Redis, Valkey, and Memcached (1.6.12+) engines.

checks.message: Replication group deletion will cause immediate cache loss
checks.context: Deleting a replication group destroys all cached data immediately. Applications will experience a cold cache and increased database load. Ensure this is planned and that the database can handle the surge.

checks.message: Disabling in-transit encryption. Cache traffic will be transmitted in plaintext
checks.context: Disabling TLS exposes all data between your application and the cache to network interception, including session tokens, cached credentials, and application data.
